data.name: Karmani
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'Karman' meaning 'to gift'. Karmani is a name of honor and esteem, bestowed upon those who are generous and gifted in their actions, whether it be in their personal or professional lives. In Islamic tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is known as 'Sahibul-Asma' or the 'Owner of Names', as he possesses all names and attributes. Karmani is a name that embodies this divine trait of bestowing blessings and gifts upon others.

in_arabic.name: كَرماني
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من كرمان، منطقة في إيران
in_arabic.long_meaning: كَرماني هو اسم مشتق من منطقة كرمان في إيران، ويعني الشخص الذي يمتلك صفات الكرم والجود. يعتبر هذا الاسم من الأسماء التي تحمل معاني قيمة في الثقافة الإسلامية، حيث يرتبط بالكرم والإنسانية.

in_urdu.name: کرمانی
in_urdu.meaning: ایران کے شہر کرمان سے متعلق
in_urdu.long_meaning: کرمانی ایک ایسا نام ہے جو ایران کے شہر کرمان سے مشتق ہے۔ یہ نام کرم و جود کی صفاتを持つ شخص کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ اسلامی ثقافت میں، یہ نام ان خصائل کو ظاہر کرتا ہے جو ایک مسلمان کے لیے ضروری ہیں، جیسے کرم، سخاوت، اور انسانیت کے ساتھ معاملات کرنا۔

in_hindi.name: करमनी
in_hindi.meaning: ईरान के शहर کرمان से संबंधित
in_hindi.long_meaning: करमनी ईरान के शहर کرمان से लिया गया एक नाम है। यह नाम करम और जूद की विशेषताओं वाले व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है। इस्लामी संस्कृति में, यह नाम उन गुणों को दर्शाता है जो एक मुसलमान के लिए आवश्यक हैं, जैसे कि करम, उदारता, और मानवता के साथ व्यवहार करना।

historical_references.context: Karmaniyya: A small Berber dynasty in the western Maghrib that held sway over Tlemcen and the surrounding region for about a century, until 1510. Ibn Khaldun describes the Karmaniyya as a dynasty of military adventurers, who, under the leadership of Ibn Abi Zar, gained control of the region and established a state centred at Tlemcen. He notes that the Karmaniyya were successful in part because they maintained a strong military, and that they were able to take advantage of the political instability that followed the decline of the Almohad caliphate.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi, The History of the Administration of Egypt, 15th century The name Karmani carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Karmaniyyun: A Berber family that ruled the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt from 1382 to 1412. Al-Maqrizi notes that the Karmaniyyun came to power following the departure of the Circassian Mamluks, who had previously held power in Egypt. He describes the Karmaniyyun as a Berber military faction that gained control of Egypt through military conquest and political maneuvering, and that they ruled Egypt during a period of relative stability and prosperity.
